lines.text: The aqueduct tunnels were cold and black, and they smelled of wet stone and twenty years of nobody.
Five of us went down. Wren, Oswin, Tamsin, me, and Ash, in the biggest robe the laundresses could find. He wore it like a tablecloth.
Two of Hobb's brickmakers led the way with a single shaded lamp. They walked those tunnels the way other men walk through their own kitchens.
We passed under the carving of the king with no rings. Tamsin held her lamp up to it, and frowned, and said nothing.
At the junction, the Order's wall stood exactly as before. Brick on brick, with seven rings stamped on every one.
Push it gently, my lord. It's only standing out of habit.
Wren and Oswin lifted the face of the wall away in one piece, and set it down without a sound. Behind it, the stolen water ran down into the dark.
Beside the channel, someone had cut stairs into the rock. Old stairs, older than the wall, worn smooth in the middle by a great many feet.
The old cistern stairs. I saw them on a map in the College library once. The map stopped at the top step. I always wondered why.
The brickmakers left us there. The older one pressed his lamp into my hands.
Bring the spectacle lady back, my lord. She told my boy his letters were very good. They weren't.
We went down. Fifty steps. A hundred. The air grew colder, and the walls began to sweat.
Above me, I felt the threads stretch. Sixty-three of them, standing on their corners in the night. And one in the upper city, sitting on a floor beside my brother.
At two hundred steps, the stairs ended at a door of black iron. Carved on it, in silver, was a single open eye.
From here on, it's the Order's house. Every corridor has a ward. Every ward has an eye. And every eye is looking for rings.
Then we're all in trouble. Except him.
He meant me. For once in my life, having nothing was going to be useful.
I put my hand on the iron door. It was so cold it burned. And somewhere far below, so faint I thought I had imagined it, I heard a sound like wind going round a chimney.
Then Tamsin whispered the password, and the iron door swung open on the vaults of the Seven.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter ninety-five, coming soon.
